headword: {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}

definitions.explanation: A victory in which the opposing team or player scores zero points or runs. Used primarily in baseball and other sports where preventing the opponent from scoring entirely is a notable achievement.

examples.japanese: ⟦エース→エース：28537_eesu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{収|おさ}めた→収める：02022_osameru⟧。
examples.english: The ace pitcher achieved a shutout victory.

examples.japanese: {今季|こんき}⟦{初|はつ}→初：10632_hatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦{全体|ぜんたい}→全体：03314_zentai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{喜|よろこ}んだ→喜ぶ：01169_yorokobu⟧。
examples.english: The whole team celebrated their first shutout victory of the season.

examples.japanese: ⟦{若手|わかて}→若手：13989_wakate⟧⟦ピッチャー→ピッチャー：09482_picchaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{強豪|きょうごう}⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見事|みごと}→見事：03744_migoto⟧な{完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{果|は}たし→果たす：10060_hatasu⟧、⟦{一躍|いちやく}→一躍：11183_ichiyaku⟧⟦スター→スター：00393_sutaa⟧になった。
examples.english: The young pitcher achieved a brilliant shutout victory against a powerhouse team and became a star overnight.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{完封|かんぷう}→完封：06543_kanpuu⟧ (shutout; holding scoreless) and ⟦{勝利|しょうり}→勝利：11795_shouri⟧ (victory). Most commonly used in baseball, where a pitcher who completes a full game without allowing any runs earns a {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}. Also used in soccer and other team sports.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{収|おさ}める→収める：02022_osameru⟧: to achieve a shutout victory
- {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{果|は}たす→果たす：10060_hatasu⟧: to accomplish a shutout victory
- {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧: to cap off with a shutout victory

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{完封|かんぷう}→完封：06543_kanpuu⟧: shutout — the act of holding the opponent scoreless
- {完封負|かんぷうま}け: shutout loss — being held scoreless
- ⟦{完投|かんとう}→完投：24619_kantou⟧: complete game — pitching the entire game (may or may not be a shutout)
- ⟦{圧勝|あっしょう}→圧勝：07903_asshou⟧: overwhelming victory — winning by a large margin, but not necessarily a shutout
